title: A Cyclone Hit 253 mph, the Fastest Gust a Weather Station Ever Logged

scenes.text: A weather station once recorded a 253 mile an hour gust.
It happened on April 10th, 1996, when Cyclone Olivia crossed Barrow Island, Australia.
That's 408 kilometres an hour, faster than most bullet trains.
Tornadoes can be stronger, but this is the highest gust ever recorded by an instrument at the surface.
At first, scientists doubted it. So a panel of experts checked the instrument.
In 2010, they made it official. It took fourteen years to prove the wind was real.

description:
On April 10th, 1996, Tropical Cyclone Olivia sent a gust of 408 kilometres an hour, 253 miles an hour, across Barrow Island.
It was verified by the World Meteorological Organization in 2010.
Could you stand in that?
first_comment: What is the strongest wind you have ever been in?
